land.text: the High Atlas around Tinmel, inside the Almoravid realm: 'Ibn Tumart abandoned his cave in 1122' and 'established his base at Tinmel' around 1124

predecessors.note: At its birth the movement held only Atlas valleys. The rest of the Almoravid land (Aghmat 1132, the Rif 1139, Tlemcen 1144, Oran 1145, Fez 1146, Marrakesh 1147) is taken by the ledger's gain events; the infobox also names the Hammadids, the Kingdom of Africa, the Banu Ghaniya, the Banu Khurasan and the second taifas as predecessors, each taken later (see ledger).

land.text: Morocco: the Marinids took Meknes (1244 or 1245), Fez (1248), Sijilmassa (1255) and Marrakesh (1269)

successors.note: The Marinids took Marrakesh in 1269, ending Almohad rule in the western Maghreb.

land.text: Ifriqiya (Tunisia, Tripolitania and eastern Algeria): the governor Abu Zakariya declared independence in 1229
the Kingdom of Tlemcen, independent around 1236

successors.note: The only Portuguese gain the Almohad page dates.

land.text: Murcia, Almeria and the rest of Almohad Spain and Portugal, 'Ibn Hud and the other local Andalusian strongmen', from October 1228

successors.note: Ibn Hud al-Mutawakkil is listed for Murcia 1228-1238 and held Almeria; the pages do not apportion the rest among the strongmen (bridge).

land.text: Valencia, taken by Zayyan ibn Mardanish after the Almohads left in 1228

successors.note: Taifa of Valencia page: 'The remaining Almohads departed and it was ... Zayyan ibn Mardanish, who took control'; it fell to Aragon on 29 September 1238.
The Almohad page's 'Mallorca in 1230 (to Aragon)'; the Las Navas page has the conquest 'from 1228 to 1232'.

capitals.name: Tinmel
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Tinmel (c. 1124-1147)'; before about 1124 the movement had no fixed seat ('Ibn Tumart abandoned his cave in 1122'). Tinmel in the High Atlas (Nfis valley).

capitals.name: Marrakesh
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Marrakesh (1147-1269)'. Second seat in Al-Andalus per the infobox: Seville 1147-1162, Cordoba 1162-1163, Seville 1163-1248; not drawn as a second dot.

rulers.name: Ibn Tumart
rulers.note: Founder, infobox 1121-1130; the List of rulers of Morocco gives 1121-1139 and Abd al-Mu'min from 1133 (overlapping).

rulers.name: Muhammad al-Nasir
rulers.note: The Almohad page's body gives 1199-1214; his own page says he died the year after Las Navas (1213).

rulers.name: Idris al-Ma'mun
rulers.note: The list starts him in 1229; the Almohad page has him abandon Seville in October 1228 and the Valencia page has him withdraw in 1228.

'For the first eight years, the Almohad rebellion was limited to a guerilla war along the peaks and ravines of the High Atlas.' The infobox gives area only for 1150 (2.3 M km2) and 1200 (2.0 M km2), none for the founding years; the 70 km radius around Tinmel is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: the High Atlas core, Aghmat (1132) and the Rif (1139)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 264,919 km2 (819 Moroccan cells, 171 Algerian cells including the Oranais) from 1139, far more than the page supports: Atlas guerilla war to 1139, then 'they expanded to the Rif mountains in the north' (1139), Taza circa 1142, Tlemcen 1144, Oran 1145, Fez 1146, Marrakesh 1147. correction.text: Cliopatria's 1147 Maghreb, without its Iberian part, plus Algeciras and Tarifa

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws all Morocco plus Andalusia, Extremadura and the Alentejo (878 cells gained over 1139) in 1147. The pages date Marrakesh 1147 ('they finally captured it in 1147'), Algeciras and Tarifa 1147, Seville 1148, Cordoba 1149 and Granada 1155, and say Muslim Spain was Almohad 'by about 1170-1172'. The correction keeps Morocco and the Algerian west as drawn and adds Algeciras; the ledger adds Seville and Cordoba in 1148-1149 and the taifas at 1152.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1152 shape without Almeria, valid for 1152-1159 (Almeria joins in 1157)

keyframe_review.note: Shape corrected for 1152-1159. It adds the Hammadid land (476 Algerian cells; 'In August 1152, he captured Bejaia, the capital of the Hammadids') and the taifas' Iberian cells, but Almeria (12 cells) was Castilian from 17 October 1147 and went to the Almohads only in 1157 (Almeria page; ledger 1157). The Norman coast (Mahdia, Sousse, Sfax, Tripoli) is not in it until 1159-1160 (ledger), after which Cliopatria's 1169 shape applies. Infobox area 2.0-2.3 M km2 for 1150-1200 against 0.66 M km2 here (ratio 0.3): the infobox counts the Sahara and Al-Andalus the grid does not; see notes.

Shape unchanged, but it holds from 1160 (Mahdia surrendered 'in January 1160'; 'Tripoli ... recognized Almohad authority right after'; 'Their rule was extended across the Maghreb by 1159'), not from 1169, and only until 1171: Murcia and Valencia join in 1172. 866,029 km2 against the infobox's 2.0-2.3 M km2 for 1150-1200 is a ratio of 0.38-0.43 (beyond a factor of two; the infobox figures are estimates that count Saharan and Iberian land the grid does not).

Shape unchanged, but it holds from 1172: 'In 1172 Murcia was taken by the Almohads' (infobox 'To the Almohads: 1172-1228'). It adds 273 Iberian cells (Albacete, Murcia, Alicante, Valencia, Castellon, Teruel), which fit Murcia and Valencia. Cliopatria's Taifa of Murcia row runs to 1176.

Shape unchanged. It loses 67 Iberian cells against 1177 (Caceres 38, Badajoz 19, Ciudad Real 4, Teruel 3, Castellon 3); no page opened dates this (Battle of Alarcos page opened on review: silent on 1188), so the ledger carries a confidence-1 bridge. The Alarcos page does date Silves (Portuguese 1189, recaptured July 1191) and the Almohad win at Alarcos on 18 July 1195 (ledger). Ifriqiya 'reconquered ... in 1187-1188' needs no change here because the shape had held it throughout.

Shape unchanged, but the 44 Caceres cells it adds belong from 1195: after the Battle of Alarcos 'the Almohads reconquered Trujillo, Montanchez, and Talavera' (ledger 1195, confidence 2, the year inferred from the battle). The other 24 cells (Badajoz 19, Ciudad Real 4, Toledo 1) are undated on every page opened (ledger 1202, confidence 1).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1202 shape, unchanged, with its 44 Caceres cells valid from 1195

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged, but the Balearic Islands it adds were taken in 1203: Abdallah ibn Ishaq was 'defeated and executed by the Almohads in 1203, who installed their own governors on the islands after this'. It holds from 1203.

The 229-cell drop (Albacete 55, Caceres 44, Jaen 29, Badajoz 29, Cordoba 22, Ciudad Real 7) is Cliopatria's reading of the aftermath of Las Navas de Tolosa (16 July 1212). The page dates only Baeza and Ubeda ('shortly after the battle'); the rest is undated on every page opened, so the 1216 date is Cliopatria's. Infobox areas do not reach this year. Review: the Almohad page dates Merida and Badajoz (1230), Cordoba (1236) and Jaen (1246) only as later Christian conquests, so the drop of those provinces' cells in 1216 is Cliopatria's and unverified.

Shape unchanged, but the Portuguese cells it drops (10 cells: Setubal 5, Evora 3, Beja 1; Alcacer do Sal lies in the Setubal district) went in 1217: 'the loss of Alcacer do Sal to the Kingdom of Portugal in 1217'. It holds from 1217.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1227 shape with the 50 Badajoz cells it drops put back, valid 1227-1228; Ifriqiya is still in it (it leaves in 1229) and all of Iberia leaves in October 1228

keyframe_review.note: Valid 1227-1228 only; replaced from 1229 by almohad-caliphate_1229. The earlier draft cut Ifriqiya from this shape at 1227 although the Hafsid page has Abu Zakariya independent only in 1229; Ifriqiya stays in until the ledger's 1229 loss. The 50 Badajoz cells Cliopatria drops against 1220 are put back: the Almohad page dates 'Merida and Badajoz in 1230 (to Leon)', after al-Ma'mun left Seville in October 1228, so they were not lost to Leon in 1227; they leave with the rest of Iberia in October 1228 (ledger). The other 27 cells of the 1227 drop (Portalegre 16, Sevilla 6, Huelva 3, Evora 1, Cordoba 1) are undated on every page opened (confidence-1 bridge, ledger 1227). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1227..1228 from this entry's own 'Valid 1227-1228 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1227 shape without Ifriqiya (Constantine and Bejaia stay to 1230) and without the Iberian mainland (the Balearic Islands stay to 1230)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1229-1235. Ifriqiya is independent under the Hafsids from 1229 (Hafsid page, 'Established: 1229'); the Almohad page ends the Almohad era in Spain in October 1228 ('The departure of al-Ma'mun in 1228 marked the end of the Almohad era in Spain') and the Valencia, Murcia and Almeria pages show Valencia, Murcia and Almeria in other hands from 1228. What remains is Morocco, the Algerian west and centre and the Balearic Islands; the ledger then removes Constantine and Bejaia (1230), Mallorca (1230), Algiers (1235) and Tlemcen (1236). Cliopatria's own 1227 shape keeps Iberia to 1235 and Ifriqiya to 1235; the Seville remnant it draws to 1248 is not supported (see notes).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1236 shape without its Iberian cells: Almohad Morocco

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria drops Ifriqiya and almost all Algeria in 1236 (1,458 cells). Pages: Ifriqiya 1229, Constantine and Bejaia 1230, Algiers 1235 (Hafsid page); Tlemcen independent 'around 1236' (Zayyanid page). The shape also keeps 288 Iberian cells (Sevilla 44, Granada 40, Beja 37, Almeria 28, Huelva 28, Cadiz 27, Faro 17, Evora 15, Cordoba 12, Setubal 8...) and the Seville remnant to 1248; the Almohad page says al-Ma'mun's departure in October 1228 'marked the end of the Almohad era in Spain', and its dated list (Cordoba 1236, Niebla-Huelva 1238, Silves 1242, Jaen 1246, Alicante 1248, Seville 1248) is of Christian conquests of land that Ibn Hud and 'other local Andalusian strongmen' held (ledger 1228). The correction removes the Iberian mainland; what is left is Morocco.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1241 shape without its Iberian cells: Almohad Morocco, valid to 1243

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1241 shape has Morocco whole and 57 Iberian cells (Sevilla 22, Faro 17, Cadiz 10, Huelva 8) of the Seville region; the correction removes the Iberian cells for the reason given on the 1236 keyframe (Almohad Spain ended in October 1228; Seville, Jaen, Silves, Alicante and the rest were conquered from Andalusi holders, 1236-1248). Morocco is not whole after 1244: Meknes 1244 or 1245 and Fez 1248 (Marinid page; ledger). The 231 Iberian cells Cliopatria drops against 1236 (Granada 40, Beja 37, Almeria 28, Malaga 24, Sevilla 22, Huelva 20, Cadiz 17, Evora 15...) are no longer an Almohad matter.

keyframe_review.note: A 1,199 km2 patch at Alicante/Elche (38.4-38.8 N, 0.67-0.22 W) labelled Almohad for 1250-1259. No page opened places the Almohads there after 1248; the Almohad page 'ultimately reduced to Marrakesh' for the last ruler. The correction is Almohad Morocco less the places the Marinid page has taken by 1248 (Meknes, Fez, Taza, Rabat, Salé), with Sijilmassa leaving in 1255 (ledger) and Marrakesh in 1269 ('Seizure of Marrakesh and the end of Almohad domination of the western Maghreb'). Bridging reading: the Almohad page says only that the last ruler was 'reduced to Marrakesh', and the pages date no further Marinid gain before 1255. Review: the Abu Yusuf Yaqub page says that in 1258 'the Almohads reduced to the southerly districts around their capital, Marrakesh', so the correction is probably too large for 1258-1268; no page dates the Marinid advance between 1248 and 1258, hence the shape stays (gap).

keyframe_review.note: The 1260-1343 rows (388,669 km2; 1,434 cells) are cell for cell the Marinid Sultanate's 1250 and 1363 shapes (Morocco and a slice of the Algerian west): Cliopatria has filed the Marinid state under the Almohad name. The Almohad dynasty ended in 1269 with the fall of Marrakesh. For 1260-1268 the correction is Almohad Morocco less Meknes, Fez, Taza, Rabat and Salé (the Marinid holdings of 1248) and, from 1255, Sijilmassa; for 1269 onward the shape belongs to the Marinid dossier (new keyframe marinid-sultanate_1269).

ledger.note: 1121: Ibn Tumart founds the Almohad movement in the High Atlas. Infobox 'Established: 1121'; his revelation came 'towards the end of Ramadan in late 1121'; 'Sometime around 1124, Ibn Tumart established his base at Tinmel'; 'For the first eight years, the Almohad rebellion was limited to a guerilla war along the peaks and ravines of the High Atlas.' The page gives no boundary; the 70 km radius is the researcher's.
1132: the Almohads conquer Aghmat. The Atlas guerilla war reaches the Haouz plain beside Marrakesh; the page lists Aghmat as 'conquered by the Almohads in 1132'.

region.text: the Rif mountains in the north

ledger.note: 1139: the Almohads expand into the Rif. 'In 1139, they expanded to the Rif mountains in the north'; Abd al-Mu'min founded a citadel and Great Mosque at Taza 'circa 1142'. The admin-1 unit Taza-Al Hoceima-Taounate is the researcher's reading of 'the Rif'.
1144: Tlemcen falls to the Almohads. The defeat of the Almoravid Tashfin 'allowed them to ... capture Tlemcen in 1144'. Cliopatria's 1139 shape already includes the Oranais.
March 1145: Oran falls and Tashfin dies. Tashfin fled to Oran and 'died in March 1145 while trying to escape'; the page does not give a separate date for the capture of Oran itself.
1146: Fez falls after a nine-month siege. The Almohads took Fez 'in 1146 after a nine-month siege'.
1147: Marrakesh falls and the Almoravid dynasty ends. The Almohads 'captured Marrakesh in 1147, after an eleven-month siege'; infobox 'Almoravids overthrown: 1147'.

region.text: Morocco as drawn in Cliopatria's 1147 shape

ledger.note: 1147: the remaining Almoravid Morocco passes to the Almohads. Bridging: no page opened dates the Sous, the Draa or the Atlantic plains; Cliopatria's 1147 shape has all of Morocco and the Almohad page says 'Their rule was extended across the Maghreb by 1159'.
1147: the capital moves from Tinmel to Marrakesh (infobox 'Marrakesh (1147-1269)').
1147: Abd al-Mu'min's army takes Algeciras and Tarifa, the first Almohad foothold in Iberia. 'In 1147 Abd al-Mu'min sent a military force' under Abu Ishaq Barraz that captured them.
1148: Seville falls to the Almohads. The city 'was captured in 1148 with local support'; the Almohad page's infobox makes Seville the Andalusian capital (1147-1162, 1163-1248).
1149: Cordoba falls to the Almohads. The Almohads 'took control of Cordoba in 1149'; the province is the researcher's reading of the city.

region.text: the Hammadid kingdom, whose capital Bejaia fell in August 1152

ledger.note: August 1152: the Almohads take Bejaia and end the Hammadid kingdom. 'In August 1152, he captured Bejaia, the capital of the Hammadids'; 'The Almohads routed them in the Battle of Setif in April 1153.' Cliopatria's shape gains 476 Algerian cells in 1152.

region.text: Granada, the last Almoravid land on the mainland

ledger.note: 1155: the last Almoravids in Granada are defeated. The Almoravids 'were defeated in 1155' and retreated to the Balearic Islands; the province of Granada is the researcher's reading.

1157: Almeria passes from Castile to the Almohads. 'Within a decade, in 1157, Almeria had passed to the control of Muslim Almohad rulers'; Alfonso VII's coalition had taken the city ('Almeria was captured on 17 October 1147') and held it through 'the decade of Christian occupation'. The earlier draft gave the Almohads Almeria in 1152 as a confidence-1 bridge from Cliopatria's Taifa of Almeria row (1147-1151), which has the city Muslim-held while the page has it Castilian. The land is the Almohad 1152 shape's Almeria cells (12), not the whole taifa shape.

1159: the Almohads take Tunis. 'Abd al-Mu'min led his forces to conquer Tunis in 1159' (Almohad page: 'In March 1159, Abd al-Mu'min led a new campaign to the east'). Tunis had paid tribute to Roger II of Sicily ('the kings of Tunis paid him tribute', Kingdom of Africa page) and was ruled by the Banu Khurasan.

region.text: the Norman coast from Sousse and Sfax to Gabes

ledger.note: 1158-1159: the Norman towns of coastal Ifriqiya are abandoned to the Almohads except Mahdia. 'All of Norman Africa was essentially abandoned to the Almohads save Mahdia'; Gabes 'was taken by force' in the siege of 1159-1160; the Almohad page has Tripoli, 'which had rebelled against the Normans two years earlier', recognise Almohad authority in 1160. The year is the page's range, the region (the Kingdom of Africa's shape minus Mahdia and Tripoli) the researcher's.

1160: Tripoli recognises Almohad authority. 'Tripoli, which had rebelled against the Normans two years earlier, recognized Almohad authority right after' the fall of Mahdia (January 1160). The Kingdom of Africa lost Tripoli to the rebels in 1158 (its dossier: counterpart 'nobody'), so the gain mirrors that.
January 1160: Mahdia surrenders and the Norman Kingdom of Africa ends. 'Mahdia was besieged soon after and surrendered in January 1160.'
1172: the Almohads take Murcia. 'In 1172 Murcia was taken by the Almohads' (infobox 'To the Almohads: 1172-1228'), ending Ibn Mardanish's kingdom; Cliopatria's Taifa of Murcia row runs to 1176.

1172: the Almohads take Valencia with Murcia. 'Valencia annexed by the Almohads in 1172' and 'Only after he died in 1172 did the Almohads take his kingdom, with little opposition' (Ibn Mardanish ruled Murcia and Valencia). Raised from a confidence-1 bridge after the Taifa of Valencia page was opened on review. Cliopatria's shape gains 40 Valencian and 23 Castellon cells in 1177.

region.text: Bougie, Constantine, Algiers and most of Tunisia

ledger.note: November 1184: the Banu Ghaniya invade and occupy the Almohad east. Ali ibn Ishaq 'invaded the eastern Maghreb in 1184'; 'The Banu Ghaniya undertook military campaigns against the Almohads in North Africa from November 1184 to 1237/1238.' The Almohad page: 'In the 1170s and 1180s, Almohad power in the eastern Maghreb was challenged by' them and the Qaraqush. The land is the one the almoravid-dynasty ledger names for the same occupation ('Bougie, Constantine and Algiers' and 'most of modern Tunisia'); the pages give no boundary. Retyped on review from contest_start: an occupation of Almohad land is an occupation in the Almohad ledger.

1185: the Almohads retake the Balearic Islands. 'In his absence, the Almohads retook the islands in 1185' (the islands had been governed by an Almoravid governor from 1126 and then by the Banu Ghaniya as independent emirs).
By 1187: the Banu Ghaniya recover the Balearics. 'Recaptured the islands from the Almohads by 1187'; Cliopatria never shows these islands Almohad before 1206.

region.text: the Extremadura cells Cliopatria's 1188 shape drops

ledger.note: 1188: Cliopatria's shape drops 67 Iberian cells held in 1177 (Caceres 38, Badajoz 19, Ciudad Real 4, Teruel 3, Castellon 3). Bridging: the Battle of Alarcos page does not mention 1188, the Almohad and Muhammad al-Nasir pages do not name these cells and no page opened dates the loss. The counterpart is a reading from Cliopatria's Kingdom of Leon row, whose 1188 shape reaches 38.6 N (shapes.csv).

region.text: Bougie, Constantine, Algiers and most of Tunisia

ledger.note: 1188: Yaqub al-Mansur reconquers Ifriqiya and the occupation ends. He 'reconquered Ifriqiya in 1187-1188'; the Banu Ghaniya raids continued to 1237/1238 (Banu Ghaniya page) and Mahdia still had a Ghaniya-linked governor in 1205-1206 (Muhammad al-Nasir page). Retyped on review from contest_end.

1189: Portugal takes Silves. 'In 1190, Almohad caliph al-Mansur traveled from North Africa to al-Andalus to invade Portugal, which had captured the city of Silves the prior year', so 1189. Cliopatria's Almohad shapes keep the Algarve throughout.
July 1191: al-Mansur recaptures Silves. 'After a campaign of approximately 15 months, al-Mansur successfully recaptured the city in July 1191.'

region.text: Trujillo and Montanchez, in Caceres province

ledger.note: 1195: after the Battle of Alarcos (18 July 1195) the Almohads take back Trujillo and Montanchez. 'The Almohads reconquered Trujillo, Montanchez, and Talavera' (Talavera lies outside the shape); the page gives no date for this beyond the battle and adds that the raids of the next two years 'did not lead to any territorial gains for the caliph'. Cliopatria draws the 44 Caceres cells only from 1202; the page puts them in 1195 at the latest. The year is inferred from the battle date; the counterpart is a reading (the page names Castile as the beaten side but not who held these towns; Cliopatria's Leon shape covers the cells).

region.text: the rest of the Extremadura cells Cliopatria's 1202 shape adds

ledger.note: 1202: Cliopatria's shape adds 24 more cells (Badajoz 19, Ciudad Real 4, Toledo 1). Bridging: the Battle of Alarcos and Muhammad al-Nasir pages do not mention them; the counterpart is a reading as for 1188.

1203: the Almohads take the Balearic Islands for good. 'Defeated and executed by the Almohads in 1203, who installed their own governors on the islands after this' (the Banu Ghaniya page; 'independent emirs until about 1203').

January 1206: Mahdia surrenders to the Almohads. 'In January 1206, in the company of the Muhammad al-Nasir, he obtained the surrender of al-Mahdia', whose governor ''Ali ibn Ghazi, cousin of Yahya, rallied to the Almohad cause'; the page's other date is the battle at Jabal Tajra in October 1205. So a Ghaniya-linked governor held Mahdia after the 1187-1188 reconquest. No page dates when the Banu Ghaniya took Mahdia or Tunis (the Banu Ghaniya page has Yahya 'active in Ifriqiya until driven out in 1226'; the Almohad page and the al-Nasir page are silent), so only this end is written and the shapes keep Ifriqiya Almohad throughout.

16 July 1212: Las Navas de Tolosa. The Almohad caliph al-Nasir is defeated; 'Shortly after the battle, the Castilians took Baeza and then conquered Ubeda' (infobox 'Fall of Ubeda and Baeza'). The land is the two towns, drawn as two 25 km circles (Baeza and Ubeda are not in the gazetteer yet, so coordinates stand in); the earlier draft took the whole province of Jaen, which the pages do not support: Jaen itself is dated only in the Almohad page's list of Christian conquests (1246, to Castile), see notes.

1216: more of the Iberian interior leaves the Almohads. Bridging Cliopatria's 229-cell drop (Albacete 55, Caceres 44, Cuenca 32, Jaen 29, Badajoz 29, Cordoba 22, Ciudad Real 7, Valencia 6, Murcia 3); the page says only that the defeat 'gave further impulse to the Christian Reconquest'. The Almohad page dates Merida and Badajoz (1230), Cordoba (1236) and Jaen (1246) only as later Christian conquests, which does not fit a 1216 loss of those provinces' cells; the attribution of these cells to Castile is Cliopatria's and unverified. The Extremadura cells (Caceres, Badajoz) belong to Leon rather than Castile.
1217: Alcacer do Sal falls to Portugal. 'The loss of Alcacer do Sal to the Kingdom of Portugal in 1217 was an exception' to the Almohad quiet after 1212.

region.text: the 27 cells outside Badajoz province that Cliopatria's 1227 shape drops

ledger.note: 1227: Cliopatria's shape drops 77 cells held in 1220: 50 in Badajoz province, which the correction puts back (the Almohad page's 'Merida and Badajoz in 1230 (to Leon)' is a Christian conquest after al-Ma'mun left Seville in October 1228, so Badajoz cannot have gone to Leon in 1227; it leaves with the rest of Iberia in October 1228, see below), and these 27 (Portalegre 16, Sevilla 6, Huelva 3, Evora 1, Cordoba 1). Bridging: no page opened dates them. The counterpart is a reading from Cliopatria's Kingdom of Portugal 1227 shape, which covers Portalegre (shapes.csv).

1228: Murcia leaves the Almohads. The infobox gives 'To the Almohads: 1172-1228' and lists '1228-1238: Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Yusuf Ibn Hud al-Mutawakkil'; the same page also says Murcia 'from 1223 to 1243 ... became the capital of an independent kingdom' (1223 is not used). Cliopatria keeps Murcia in the Almohad shape to 1235. The Almohad page's 'Murcia in 1243 (to Castile)' is the later conquest of Ibn Hud's kingdom ('under the Treaty of Alcaraz swore fealty to Castille'), not an Almohad loss.

1228: Almohad rule in Valencia ends. 'The remaining Almohads departed and it was a descendant of Ibn Mardanish, Zayyan ibn Mardanish, who took control', after a rebellion 'in late 1228 or early 1229'; 'the Almohad caliph Idris al-Ma'mun withdrew from the region in 1228'. Valencia then falls to Aragon on 29 September 1238 ('The city surrendered on 29 September'; the Las Navas page says 28 September), a conquest of Zayyan's taifa, not of the Almohads: the earlier draft recorded it as an Almohad loss (1238) from the Almohad page's list. The year is the page's either-or (late 1228 or early 1229).

1228: Almeria passes from the Almohads to Ibn Hud. The page heads Almohad rule over the city '1157-1228/1238' and says 'Almeria submitted to the authority of Ibn Hud', who 'pledged nominal allegiance to Abbasid authorities by 1228'; 'After Ibn Hud's assassination in Almeria in 1238' it went to the Emirate of Granada ('to which Almeria belonged from then on'). 1228 follows the Almohad page's end of Almohad rule in Spain; the page's range 1228/1238 leaves 1238 open.

region.text: the rest of Almohad Spain and Portugal

ledger.note: October 1228: Almohad rule in Iberia ends. 'In October 1228, with Spain practically all lost, al-Ma'mun abandoned Seville' and 'The departure of al-Ma'mun in 1228 marked the end of the Almohad era in Spain'; 'Ibn Hud and the other local Andalusian strongmen were unable to stem the rising flood of Christian attacks'. The Almohads hold nothing on the Iberian mainland after this (the Valencia, Murcia and Almeria pages agree); the Balearic Islands are kept to 1230 below. The infobox capital 'Seville (1163-1248)' and the 1248 'ex-Almohad capital' are the city's last year, not Almohad rule. The land is Cliopatria's 1227 shape on the mainland (with the 50 Badajoz cells put back) less Murcia, Valencia and Almeria. The page names no holder of the rest; the counterpart is the one ruler the pages name (Ibn Hud, shown in the Taifa of Murcia row 1228-1238), a bridge. Later fates, as the Almohad page lists them (Christian conquests of this land, not Almohad losses): Merida and Badajoz 1230 (to Leon), Beja 1234 (Portugal), Cordoba 1236 (Castile), Niebla-Huelva 1238 (Leon), Silves 1242 (Portugal), Murcia 1243 (Castile), Jaen 1246 (Castile), Alicante 1248 (Castile), Seville 22 December 1248 (Castile); Granada, which 'alone would remain independent', under the Nasrids.

1229: Ifriqiya breaks away. The governor Abu Zakariya, 'initially appointed governor of the region by the Almohad caliph', repudiated al-Ma'mun's authority in 1229 'and declared himself independent' (infobox 'Established: 1229'). He took the caliphal title only in 1236 or 1237. The region leaves out Constantine and Bejaia, which the next event dates to 1230 (the 'Ifriqiya' region reaches them).
1230: Constantine and Bejaia go to the Hafsids. 'Abu Zakariya annexed Constantine (Qusantina) and Bejaia (Bijaya) in 1230.'

1230: Mallorca falls to Aragon. The Almohad page lists 'Mallorca in 1230 (to Aragon)'; the Las Navas page has James I conquering the Balearics 'from 1228 to 1232'. Whether the islands' Almohad governors still obeyed the caliph after October 1228 is on no page opened, hence confidence 2: the islands are kept Almohad to 1230 as the page lists them, though the page says the Almohad era in Spain ended in 1228.

region.text: Algiers as far as the Chelif River

ledger.note: 1235: Algiers falls to the Hafsids. 'In 1235 he captured Algiers and then established his authority as far as the Chelif River.' The units Alger and Chlef are the researcher's reading; the page does not say from whom he took it.

region.text: the Kingdom of Tlemcen, without Algiers and the Chelif

ledger.note: 1236: Tlemcen becomes independent under the Zayyanids. 'On the collapse of the Almohad Caliphate's rule around 1236 ... the Kingdom of Tlemcen became independent under the rule of the Zayyanids' (the infobox gives 1235). The land is Cliopatria's Zayyanid 1236 shape less Alger and Chlef, which went to the Hafsids in 1235 (event above) and which the shape overlaps (it reaches 4.67 E); the Zayyanid found event names the Oranais.
1244: the Marinids take Meknes. 'Meknes was captured in 1244 or 1245'; the Marinid page's header gives the dynasty as 1244-1465.

By 1248: the Marinids take Taza, Rabat and Salé. 'Between 1244 and 1248 the Marinids were able to take Taza, Rabat, Salé, Meknes and Fez from the weakened Almohads'; the page gives the span 1244-1248, not a year for each, so 1248 is the span's end.
1248: the Marinids take Fez. 'Fez was captured in 1248' and the page adds that the Marinid ruler 'established his capital in Fes'; the Almohad infobox also dates 'Marinid suzerainty: 1248'.
1255: the Marinids take Sijilmassa. 'Fez was captured in 1248, and Sijilmassa in 1255.'

minus.text: Meknes, Fez, Taza, Rabat and Salé, the places the Marinids took from the Almohads in 1244-1248
Cliopatria's Almohad Morocco of 1260 without the places the Marinids had taken by 1248

union.text: Marrakesh, where the last Almohad ruler was killed in 1269

region.text: Almohad Morocco outside the places already lost and Marrakesh

ledger.note: 1269: the rest of Almohad Morocco passes to the Marinids with Marrakesh. Bridging: the Marinid page dates Meknes 1244/1245, Taza, Rabat and Salé 1244-1248, Fez 1248, Sijilmassa 1255 and Marrakesh 1269, but names no year for the Atlantic plains, the Atlas or the Souss; Cliopatria draws all Morocco as Marinid-sized from 1260 under the Almohad name. On review the Abu Yusuf Yaqub page adds: in 1258 'the Almohads reduced to the southerly districts around their capital, Marrakesh', which would make the shape too large for 1258-1268; it dates no Marinid gain before Marrakesh (8 September 1269) except the Draa valley (1271), Sijilmassa (1274, against 1255 on the Marinid page) and the last Almohad remnants at Tinmel (1276). The date stays 1269 to match the Marinid ledger.

region.text: Marrakesh, where the last Almohad ruler was killed in 1269

ledger.note: 1269: the Marinids take Marrakesh and the Almohad Caliphate ends. Timeline 'Seizure of Marrakesh and the end of Almohad domination of the western Maghreb' (1269); the Almohad page: the last ruler Idris al-Wathiq 'was ultimately reduced to Marrakesh, where he was killed in 1269'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1269'. Cliopatria carries the Almohad name on a Marinid-sized shape to 1343. The Abu Yusuf Yaqub page: Abu Yusuf 'entered Marrakesh on 8 September 1269, putting a final end to the Almohad Caliphate'.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of the Almoravid realm
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: the Almoravids crushed the Almohads at al-Buhayra in April or May 1130, Ibn Tumart died in August 1130, then Aghmat fell in 1132, Tlemcen in 1144, Fez in 1146 and Marrakesh in 1147.
wars.note: Dates from the Almohad page; the Almoravid last stand at Oran is March 1145.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of Al-Andalus
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: 'Between 1146 and 1173, the Almohads gradually wrested control'; Algeciras 1147, Seville 1148, Cordoba 1149, Granada 1155, Murcia 1172.
wars.note: Spans 'Muslim Spain had fallen under their control by about 1170-1172' (Almohad page).

wars.name: Almohad conquest of the Hammadids and Norman Africa
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: Bejaia August 1152, Setif April 1153 (a rout of the Arab tribes), Tunis March 1159, Mahdia January 1160, Tripoli 1160.

wars.name: Banu Ghaniya campaigns in Ifriqiya and the Balearics
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: Ifriqiya reconquered 1187-1188; Balearics retaken 1185, lost again by 1187, taken for good in 1203; raids continue to 1237/1238; Mahdia surrenders in January 1206 after the October 1205 battle at Jabal Tajra (Muhammad al-Nasir page).
wars.note: The land of the 1184-1188 occupation is recorded in both ledgers as occupation_start/end.

wars.name: Almohad campaigns against Portugal and Castile (Silves, Alarcos)
wars.outcome: Almohad victories: Silves, taken by Portugal in 1189, recaptured by al-Mansur in July 1191 after a campaign of about 15 months; Alarcos, 18 July 1195, after which 'the Almohads reconquered Trujillo, Montanchez, and Talavera'; the raids of 1195-1197 'did not lead to any territorial gains for the caliph'.

wars.name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
wars.outcome: Christian victory on 16 July 1212: al-Nasir withdrew to Marrakesh; Baeza and Ubeda fell shortly after; 'By 1252 the Almohad empire was almost finished.'
wars.note: Allies of Castile are not recorded here because the page text read for this dossier was asked only for the aftermath.

wars.name: Marinid conquest of Morocco

zones.text: Marrakesh, where the last Almohad ruler was killed in 1269

wars.outcome: Marinid victory: Meknes 1244 or 1245, Fez 1248, Sijilmassa 1255, Marrakesh 1269.
wars.note: The Marinid page's timeline begins 'The Banu Marin (Marinids) attacks the Almohads' in 1215 and has Abd al-Haqq I die 'during victorious combat against the Almohads' in 1217.

wars.name: Christian conquests in Almohad Spain
wars.outcome: Christian gains: Alcacer do Sal 1217 and Mallorca 1230 (the Balearics 1228-1232 on the Las Navas page). After al-Ma'mun abandoned Seville in October 1228 the Almohads held nothing on the Iberian mainland; the later conquests (Cordoba 1236, Valencia 1238, Seville 22 December 1248...) were made against Ibn Hud, Zayyan ibn Mardanish and the other Andalusi rulers, not against the Almohads.
wars.note: Recast on review; the page also says the departure of al-Ma'mun in 1228 'marked the end of the Almohad era in Spain'.

certainty.note: An Atlas guerilla zone and then a patchwork of conquered towns; the pages give cities, never frontiers.

Approximate frontiers throughout: the Saharan edge, the Castilian and Portuguese frontier (soft though a truce was bought from Ferdinand III for 300,000 maravedis), and the Ifriqiya-Libya limit. No treaty line is given on any page.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROWS. (1) 'Almohad Caliphate' 1260-1343 (three shapes, 388,669 / 388,541 km2) is cell for cell the Marinid Sultanate's 1250 and 1363 shape; the Almohad state ended in 1269. All three are 'wrong' here and should be reassigned to marinid-sultanate. (2) The 1250-1259 shape is a 1,199 km2 patch at Alicante/Elche that no page supports. (3) The 1139 shape is far larger than the Atlas and Rif the page gives. (4) The corrections for 1250-1268 keep Almohad Morocco less the Marinid holdings of 1248 (a bridging reading, confidence 1 at 1269); the Abu Yusuf Yaqub page says that in 1258 the Almohads were 'reduced to the southerly districts around their capital', so even that shape is probably too large. (5) Cliopatria's shapes 1227-1241 keep Iberia to 1235 and the Seville remnant to 1248; the pages do not (next paragraph).

IBERIA AFTER 1228 (repair pass of 2026-10-19; replaces the first draft's reading). Which parts of al-Andalus stayed Almohad after 1228: none, on the pages opened. Almohad Caliphate page: 'In October 1228, with Spain practically all lost, al-Ma'mun abandoned Seville' and 'The departure of al-Ma'mun in 1228 marked the end of the Almohad era in Spain'; 'Ibn Hud and the other local Andalusian strongmen were unable to stem the rising flood of Christian attacks'. The list that follows (Merida and Badajoz 1230 to Leon, Mallorca 1230 to Aragon, Beja 1234 to Portugal, Cordoba 1236 to Castile, Valencia and Niebla-Huelva 1238, Silves 1242, Murcia 1243, Jaen 1246, Alicante 1248, Seville 22 December 1248) is a list of Christian conquests, and the page calls Seville the 'ex-Almohad capital'. The Taifa of Valencia page has the Almohads leave Valencia in 1228 and Zayyan ibn Mardanish rule it until its surrender to Aragon on 29 September 1238; the Taifa of Murcia page has Murcia leave the Almohads in 1228 for Ibn Hud and swear fealty to Castile in 1243; the Almeria page has the city submit to Ibn Hud. So the first draft (Cordoba, Valencia, the south of Iberia and Seville recorded as Almohad losses of 1236-1248, using the list selectively) was wrong. The review's fixes that date Badajoz 1230, Beja 1234, Niebla-Huelva 1238, Silves 1242, Jaen 1246 and Alicante 1248 as Almohad losses are NOT applied as such: those places fell from Andalusi holders to the Christian kingdoms, so they belong in the ledgers of Castile, Leon, Portugal and Aragon (eu-12) and appear here only as the 'later fates' in the October 1228 event. What the dossier does now: the corrections remove the Iberian mainland from 1229 (new keyframe _1229, then the 1236 and 1241 shapes); the Badajoz cells stay to October 1228 (keyframe 1227); Murcia, Valencia and Almeria are separate 1228 losses; the rest of Iberia goes in October 1228 to Ibn Hud (counterpart taifa-of-murcia, a bridge: no page names another strongman or apportions the land). The Balearic Islands are kept to 1230 as the page lists Mallorca (confidence 2: whether the island governors still obeyed the caliph is on no page). The infobox capital 'Seville (1163-1248)' and 'Marinid suzerainty: 1248' are the capital's last year, not Almohad rule. Disagreement kept in view: the Taifa of Murcia page also calls Murcia 'the capital of an independent kingdom' from 1223, against 'To the Almohads: 1172-1228'.

AREA. The infobox gives 2.3 M km2 (1150, high-end peak estimate) and 2.0 M km2 (1200, low-end peak estimate); Cliopatria's peak is 949,022 km2 (1206) and the shapes alive in those years are 504,938 km2 (1147, ratio 0.22) and 925,048 km2 (1188, ratio 0.46). The grid counts the land cells of the named regions and omits the Saharan interior the infobox includes; the shapes were left standing and the ratio is flagged on the 1152 and 1169 verdicts.

OTHER PAGE CONFLICTS. The Las Navas page dates the Balearic conquest 1228-1232, the Almohad page Mallorca 1230. Valencia surrendered on 28 September 1238 (Las Navas) or 29 September (Taifa of Valencia). Sijilmassa fell in 1255 (Marinid page) or submitted in 1274 (Abu Yusuf Yaqub page). Ibn Tumart reigned 1121-1130 (Almohad infobox) or 1121-1139, Abd al-Mu'min from 1130 or 1133 (List of rulers of Morocco); al-Nasir 1199-1214 (Almohad body) or 1213 (his page and the list). The Almohad page's 'Marinid suzerainty: 1248' is unexplained.

OTHER REPAIRS (repair pass). Algiers and the Chelif are lost once, to the Hafsids in 1235; the 1236 Zayyanid loss is the Zayyanid shape less Alger and Chlef. The Banu Ghaniya invasion of 1184-1188 is an occupation (occupation_start/end, counterpart almoravid-dynasty, the Almoravid ledger's region), not a contest. Almeria was Castilian from 17 October 1147 and Almohad in 1157 (Almeria page), not in 1152. Silves was Portuguese in 1189 and recaptured in July 1191; Alarcos was won on 18 July 1195 and Trujillo and Montanchez reconquered (Battle of Alarcos page). Mahdia surrendered in January 1206 (Muhammad al-Nasir page). Valencia in 1172 is dated by the Taifa of Valencia page. Baeza and Ubeda replace the whole province of Jaen in 1212. Rulers: the fourteen Almohad reigns of the List of rulers of Morocco.

NOT SETTLED (page silent, no event written, or confidence 1): the Almohad conquest of Jaen (1168) and the Algarve; the other 1152 taifa gains (Badajoz, Niebla, Saltes, Carmona, Cordoba, Denia and Tejada are confidence-1 bridges at 1152); the Qaraqush and Zengid hold on Tripolitania and Gabes in the 1170s; Ceuta, Sale, the Sous and the Draa under Abd al-Mu'min; Cliopatria's Extremadura changes of 1188, 1202 and 1227 beyond Trujillo and Montanchez (1195); the start of the Banu Ghaniya hold on Mahdia and Tunis after 1188; the Tunisian governors 1207-1229; the rest of Morocco in 1147 and 1269; who held Jaen, Cordoba, Granada, Malaga and Seville between 1228 and their fall.

COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER: 'Banu Khurasan (Tunis)' (1059-1159); the Banu Ghaniya in Ifriqiya ('Banu Ghaniya', 1184-1237; their Balearic emirate is recorded under almoravid-dynasty, as that dossier does). Ibn Hud's emirate (1228-1238) is carried by taifa-of-murcia and Zayyan ibn Mardanish's by taifa-of-valencia (both eu-12). GAZETTEER NAMES: Tinmel and Aghmat are given as coordinates; Baeza and Ubeda are two 25 km circles given as coordinates (add both as places).
